thread:
PagerBot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 alert for dedicated cluster 'us-west-2-pool-7' (customer: kestrelanalytics). Error rate spike detected on tenant_id=kestrel-123 — 5xx / gateway timeouts increasing rapidly. Pager: SRE on-call nina.

nina: ack, I'm on it. seeing alert: 5xx rate 18% over last 5m, p95 latency 3.6s, tail at 120s. customer reports timeouts. tagging @kestrel-support.

kestrel-support: thanks, we're seeing a flood of failed inference calls from our front-end, most responses are 502/504. Customers on our side are seeing slow UI loads. Impacting ~40% of requests.

sam: nina can you paste the metric queries you used? I'll start checking gateway logs and routing.

nina: PromQL: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="kestrel-123",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="kestrel-123"}[5m]))` -> 0.18. Also `avg_over_time(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~"pool-7.*"}[5m])` shows GPU util at 98% on pool node gpu-07.

li: copying gateway logs from last 2m:
```
2026-03-14T17:34:02Z gateway usw2-gw-3 kestrel-123 req_id=abc123 status=502 upstream_error=timeout backend=runtime-pod-45
2026-03-14T17:34:04Z gateway usw2-gw-2 kestrel-123 req_id=def456 status=504 upstream_error=kvcache-miss
2026-03-14T17:34:06Z gateway usw2-gw-3 kestrel-123 req_id=ghi789 status=502 upstream_error=gpu-saturation
```

li: baseline for other tenants on pool-7 is normal, looks like tenant kestrel-123 is saturating KV-cache and GPU memory. Potential noisy neighbor or very high batch sizes.

jordan: @nina we have a recent rollback safepoint and a canary model pinned for kestrel. Are they pinned to a heavy unquantized vm?

nina: They recently switched to model: biggen-7b-unq v2 in their config (rolled 30m ago). That would explain memory. Config excerpt from tenant config: `model: biggen-7b-unq, max_batch: 64, kv_cache_enabled: true, prefetched_sequences: 4096`.

sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle tenant concurrency via routing layer 2) set model fallback to quantized variant 3) evict tenant from pool-7 and rehome to burst pool / dedicated spare nodes 4) increase pool capacity (spin up spare GPUs). Which to try first?

nina: Do 1 + 2 now. If no improvement in 5m, do 3. I'll coordinate with kestrel-support to confirm fallback.

nina: Applying routing throttle: `POST /admin/routing/throttle {"tenant":"kestrel-123","max_concurrency":10}` -> accepted.

ops-bot: Command executed: throttle applied to tenant kestrel-123 at gateway routing layer.

nina: Applying model fallback: `PATCH /tenants/kestrel-123/config {"model_fallback":"biggen-7b-q4"}`. Keep KV cache enabled but reduce max_batch to 8.

ops-bot: Patch applied. Config change will take ~20s to hit new runtime workers.

kestrel-support: Confirmed we accept fallback to quantized model. Some requests may change latency profile but acceptable to reduce errors.

li: Observing immediate metric shift: 5xx rate down from 18% -> 6% after throttle + fallback within 90s. GPU util dropped from 98% -> 73% on impacted nodes.

jordan: Nice. Still seeing intermittent 502s from gateway on node gpu-07. Might be residual connections / queued requests. Suggest we also evict tenant from pool-7 to isolate. Any spare nodes in us-west-2?

sam: We have 2 spare dedicated nodes in us-west-2-burst (gpu-burst-01/02). I'll prepare migration.

nina: Initiating live eviction + rehome: `POST /admin/tenants/rehome {"tenant":"kestrel-123","target_pool":"us-west-2-burst"}`. This will start draining sessions and reestablishing workers. Expected downtime for in-flight sessions ~30s-90s. Notifying customer.

kestrel-support: Acknowledged. Please give a 2-min heads up before rehome. We'll pause critical traffic for 30s during the handoff.

ops-bot: Rehome job queued: job_id=rehome-7861. Draining 12 workers.

li: While draining, I see one runtime pod repeatedly OOMing with CUDA OOM. Log snippet: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory allocating 1.2GiB` on runtime-pod-45. That pod has been the noisy process.

nina: OK, mark runtime-pod-45 as unhealthy and evict. `kubectl label pod runtime-pod-45 evict=true --context=cluster-usw2` -> OK. Controllers will replace with new pod on burst pool.

ops-bot: Pod runtime-pod-45 marked for eviction. Replacement triggered.

sam: Migration progressing. Rehome job status: draining -> migrating weights -> reattach KV cache -> completed. job_id=rehome-7861 status=completed at 17:37:12Z.

li: Post-migration metrics: 5xx rate for kestrel-123 now 0.6%, p95 latency 210ms. GPU util on pool-7 back to normal 45%. Burst nodes reporting 40% util.

kestrel-support: We're seeing a big improvement on our side. UI errors dropped to <1%. Thanks for the quick action and heads up.

nina: Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep monitoring for 30m. On-call handoff: I'll be handing off to @sam in 20m; sam please take lead for postmortem.

sam: Taking handoff. I'll open a ticket and coordinate RCA. Initial notes: root cause likely tenant change to heavy unquantized model + high batch config triggering GPU OOM and KV pressure. Immediate fixes: throttle, fallback, rehome.

jordan: Suggest follow-up action items: 1) add guardrail preventing auto-rollouts to unquantized big models on Dedicated pools without spike-protection 2) autoscaling policy to reserve N spare GPUs for bursts 3) tenant-level admission control that caps max_batch when memory high 4) clearer customer doc for model size warnings.

nina: +1 on all. I'll create TODOs and tag product and runtime teams.

ops-bot: Incident SEV-2 -> Mitigated. Incident will remain open for postmortem until tasks closed.

sam: Posting short incident summary for customers and execs: `Mitigation: routing throttle + model fallback + rehome to burst nodes. Impact: kestrelanalytics experienced 5xx/timeouts for ~18min, peak 18% error rate, now reduced to <1%. Root cause: tenant config changed to unquantized large model causing GPU OOM and KV pressure on pool-7. Next actions: guardrails and autoscale. Owner: sam (postmortem).`

kestrel-support: Appreciate the quick response. We'll coordinate internal postmortem and send a customer note.

nina: closing here — will ping when postmortem is up. :white_check_mark:
